sources.note: Nothing on Mimi-N. Sec. 2.3 (p.6) lists the three 'Mimi' sources (Decorse 1907, Lukas & Voelckers 1939, Jungraithmayr 1971) and calls Nachtigal's Mimi 'mysterious and still not clearly affiliated'; sec. 4.3 'Tones' concerns Maba and Aiki only; the word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: Starostin, George. 2011. On Mimi. Journal of Language Relationship 6: 115-140.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative/lexicostatistical study of Mimi-N and Mimi-D vs Maban; reproduces Nachtigal's Mimi-N forms (via Lukas & Voelckers 1938), a few of which carry acute marks (e.g. imperatives z=áia 'come!', z=úlko 'leave!', p.~125), but never says what the marks denote; explicitly states that grammatical data are unknown for both Mimis (p.117). No occurrence of 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' in the text.
